turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr. Hale, come on in. Sorry the vent sticks, it's a little warm in here.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. It is no trouble at all, and I appreciate you fitting me in.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): The slip just says elbow. Tell me in your own words what has been going on.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The outer side of my right elbow has been painful for six weeks.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm Dan, his caregiver, I stay over at the house. He's been guarding that arm the whole time.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're a carpenter, from the referral, is that right?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I hang doors, and I paint the trim as well. It began on a kitchen job.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): What makes the pain worse?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Lifting a cup, more than anything. A coffee mug, or even a gallon of paint. I would put it at a 6 out of 10 then.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): And when the arm is just resting, does it go quiet?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): A dull ache remains. The sharp part is the grip.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He sleeps badly too. I'm up with him, he's pacing half the night.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I must respectfully disagree. I sleep. I feel the elbow only if I roll onto that side, and then I drift off again.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. You two don't match on the nights, so I'll keep both versions. What are you taking for the pain?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Ibuprophen, by mouth. 400 milligrams, three times a day, with food. I have taken it through these six weeks.
[SEG0016] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He does not take the tablets on Sundays. I fill the box, and Sunday is always left.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Forgive me, that is not right. It is Saturdays, not Sundays. I am off on Saturday, and I forget the midday dose.

[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Saturdays, then, not Sunday, so three times a day with Saturday slipping. Err, thinking out loud, outer elbow in a carpenter, worse with a cup for six weeks, that is the tendon origin, lateral epicondylitis, but I want the exam to agree before I lock it in.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tender, right on the lateral epicondyle. Resisted wrist extension brings the pain right back. I don't see any swelling, and the elbow flexes and straightens fully.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. That is the spot.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any swelling you've noticed at home, at the end of the day?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It does not swell.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does the hand go numb, or tingle?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. I won't call that numbness, it's too soft. Any neck pain? The neck can throw pain down the arm.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My neck is not painful.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): One more odd one. Any wound that has been slow to heal? It only matters if we ever inject.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He caught a knuckle on a chisel last month. The cut healed in five days.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that is accurate. Five days, and it looked quite normal.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Healing isn't slow, then. Are you off the tools completely?
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He hasn't worked in two weeks. I made him stay in.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I have been doing light work, sanding and fitting hardware. I have given up the heavy lifting.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): So light duty, not a full stop. Uh, before the plan, the nurse checked you in the hall?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): She did. She said my pressure was 138 over 84.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): And she wrote the same number, 138 over 84, pulse 72. That's today's reading. I'm not worried about the pressure.
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He watches those numbers because his father had a heart attack.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. My father had a heart attack at age seventy-two. I myself have not.

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted, his father, a heart attack. Let me pull the threads. My working impression is lateral epicondylitis, and I can't completely exclude a mild inflammatory arthritis without a film and a blood test, so that stays a side possibility, not the lead.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. Please tell me how you would like to proceed.

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Get a counterforce brace, the band just below the tender point, and wear it when you grip or paint. Ice the area for, uh, ten minutes after work, not twenty, ten is enough. Leave the heavy cans to someone else.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I will purchase the brace today. The ice is simple enough.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep the ibuprophen, 400 milligrams by mouth three times a day with food, and put a reminder on Saturday so that dose is not missed. No new pill from me.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Very well.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): No injection today. If it does not settle with the brace and the therapy, we might consider a steroid injection later. I don't want to jump there.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): I would prefer to avoid an injection if we can. Thank you.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll refer you to physical therapy for an elbow program. And I'll see you back in two weeks.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is quite manageable.

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thursday morning at eight, two things are booked. The nurse takes blood for a CRP, and we x-ray the right elbow the same morning. No fasting, and take your morning ibuprofen as usual.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday at eight. No fasting, and I take the ibuprofen. I have it.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): If those are borderline, we do the third test, an ultrasound of the tendon. Only if the x-ray or the CRP is borderline. I'm not booking the ultrasound now.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The east lot is a mess on Thursdays. We'll just use the garage.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Garage, yeah. Anything you wanted to add, Mr. Hale?
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): No. You have explained it clearly, and I am grateful.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): All right. We'll see what Thursday shows and go from there.

spec.situation: Painter or carpenter with outer elbow pain for six weeks, worse lifting a cup; takes ibuprofen; physio and brace advice; no injection yet.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Medication, dose, route, frequency, duration supported; exact current use is imperfect because Saturday midday dose is missed.

bad.reason: Value is supported, but patient first reported it; not solely reported_by doctor.
CRP is planned by doctor, but indication 'exclude inflammatory arthritis' is implied, not explicitly tied to CRP alone.
bad.text: CRP blood test (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=Exclude inflammatory arthritis)

bad.reason: Saturday missed dose conflict is resolved by patient correction; not unresolved.
bad.text: Ibuprofen is taken three times a day, but the midday dose is missed on Saturdays; the caregiver first said Sundays and the patient corrected the day to Saturday. (type=adherence_uncertain, related_entities=medications[0], resolution_status=unresolved)
